title: pvExtractTimeSteps
body:
## pvExtractTimeSteps

Restricts a time-varying input to selected time steps, given as listed zero-based indices (Select Time Steps, ParaView default) or as an inclusive index range with a stride (Select Time Range). Downstream nodes see only those steps: a request for an unselected time is answered by a selected step chosen by ApproximationMode (Nearest Time Step by default), and times outside the selection get the first or last selected step. Use it to thin a long transient before temporalStatistics or pvParticlePath, or to hold a branch at one step.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Indices are positions in the input's time list, not time values; indices beyond the last step are ignored without warning.
- Scene times are still chosen by the Schemaxis times setting; this node only maps them onto the selected steps.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ExtractTimeSteps`. Identity: `filters/ExtractTimeSteps`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: any data object (vtkDataObject). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataObject"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ApproximationMode` | If the scene's time does not match the time in any of the timesteps selected (likely because something else in the scene has time steps at different times) this setting controls which timestep should be returned by the filter. The options are the previous time step, the nearest time step and the next time step. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Previous Time Step","Next Time Step","Nearest Time Step"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Previous Time Step"` |
| `SelectionMode` | Extract time steps supports two ways to select the time steps to be extracted: - **Select Time Steps**: Specify time steps to be extracted by their index - **Select Time Range**: Specify the start and end time steps of a range by their index and optionally specify a stride to optionally take every nth timestep in the range. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Select Time Steps","Select Time Range"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Select Time Steps"` |
| `TimeStepIndices` | This property specifies the indices of the time steps to extract. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |
| `TimeStepInterval` | Select the stride to use when extracting the range of time steps (the n in every nth timestep). | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `TimeStepRange` | Select the beginning and end indices of the range of timesteps to extract. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json

  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvExtractTimeSteps",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
